name: Nell Graves
life: “My first wedding assignment was my parents marrying each other a second time.” On Tuesday, near the corner outside Coastal Barber, Nell usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I've come to photograph the three waistlines. My own wedding pictures show nothing below our shoulders.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. Nell has a scattering of freckles across the bridge of the nose, with a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. Nell looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry during a conversation.
personality: Nell carries anger into a conversation very slowly. Once it arrives, a quiet statement of facts can be considerably harder to sidestep than a shout.
agenda: To photograph all three women's changes to the same garment.
family: Toby Diaz is Nell’s half-sibling. Nell brings a spare shopping bag. Toby chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The clean ledger*, Toby says, “I sell drugs and used to think settling money settled everything.”
connections: Parker Cho. They photograph the original chalk before the hem is washed.

reactions.situation: A relative asks to hide the changed seam
reactions.response: Nell asks the bride herself what should show above the hem.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Nell offers to help correct the printed name and leaves it to the colleague whether any public explanation is wanted.

reactions.situation: If a friend asks for a false alibi for an ordinary missed appointment
reactions.response: Nell offers to accompany them while they tell the truth.
